svg.text: BEGINNER • EXAM REVISION | Models, uncertainty, and customer-churn insights
Estimate the pattern; inspect uncertainty; never confuse association with cause.
Arrows mean sequence/flow; they do not imply causation.
One number from a sample estimates
ML: inputs X map to target Y.
choose parameter values that maximize it.
x = observed data • θ = model parameters
MATCH THE DATA PATTERN TO THE QUESTION
CHURN EDA: FROM DATA TO FINDING
• Credit-card users were less likely to churn.
• Short-tenure customers were more likely to churn.
• Pair plot: tenure, monthly usage, revenue, CLV by churn.
• Hexbin: tenure vs monthly charges shows concentrations.
Fields: account/customer traits, revenue, satisfaction, CLV.
Qualitative plot readings only: no exact rates, tests, or causal proof supplied.
Association is a clue to investigate—not proof that a feature causes churn.
Parameter treated as fixed; estimates use data.
No prior distribution for parameter estimate.
Prior = initial parameter distribution. Posterior = updated
distribution after data; prior knowledge can contribute.
• A point estimate is not the full uncertainty story.
• Match distribution to data; they are not interchangeable.
• Prior ≠ posterior; wide interval ≠ precise estimate.
• CLT: “enough data” is not a full set of conditions.
Parameter: population property; estimate: sample value
SE: uncertainty / sampling variability of estimate*
Log-normal: right-skew; log values become normal
Exponential: wait time • Poisson: event count
MLE: θ̂ = arg maxθ L(θ | x)
1 Estimation vs inference: what extra does inference examine?
2 What trade-off comes with a parametric model?
3 What parameter values does MLE choose?
4 Exponential vs Poisson: what does each model?
5 Why does a wide confidence interval matter?
6 Prior vs posterior: what changes after data arrive?
9 Why is an EDA relationship not causal proof?
10 What does CLV estimate; which inputs are named?
1 Estimate = point value; inference adds population/process interpretation + uncertainty.
2 Finite structure can be faster/easier, but assumptions constrain patterns.
3 Values that maximize the likelihood of observed data.
4 Exponential = waiting time; Poisson = event count in fixed interval.
5 It allows a wider range of plausible effects; uncertainty is greater.
6 Prior is initial; posterior is updated after observed data.
8 Converts tenure into five equal-width categories.
9 Plots show association; they do not establish cause.
10 Customer value over lifetime; expected duration and spending.
